reader.decision: Turn on `touch_on_request` in production (set it to true in config/prod.yaml). Do not move the touch into `auth-service` now.
reader.decision_reason: The message confirms the cause: edge-proxy only calls touch when the flag is true, the flag is false in prod, and nothing else updates last_seen_at. Flipping the existing flag is the smallest fix that targets that cause. The timezone theory is ruled out.

reconstruction.problem: Users are logged out about 30 minutes after login even while active. session-gc runs every 10 minutes and deletes rows where last_seen_at is older than the 30-minute IDLE_LIMIT. Nothing updates last_seen_at after login, because edge-proxy/session.py calls auth_client.touch only when touch_on_request is true, and config/prod.yaml sets it to false.
reconstruction.what_breaks: Active sessions look idle to session-gc, so it deletes them. Users land on the login page in the middle of their work. The timezone-mismatch theory is wrong: the cutoff is timezone-aware and last_seen_at is timestamptz.
reconstruction.fix: Set touch_on_request to true in production so edge-proxy touches last_seen_at on each request. The alternative is to move the touch into auth-service.

follow_up_questions: What is the cost of turning on touch_on_request in production? For example, what is the extra load on auth-service or the database from a touch call on every request?
What does moving the touch into auth-service involve, and what would it give us over the flag?
reader.closing_answer: I turn on `touch_on_request` in production. The message does not state the cost of either option, so I would check the extra touch load on auth-service before rollout. I would revisit moving the touch into auth-service only if that load is a problem.
